title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is the start of a letter to him, almost certainly from Pierre Deligne. The salutation reads 'Cher Schurik', Shurik being the Russian diminutive of Alexander. The previous page is signed 'Pierre' and contains Russian about 'Lena', Deligne's wife Elena. The letter answers questions Grothendieck had raised while working on the 'Teichmüller'/anabelian programme of 1981. The previous page sketches why every open subgroup of Gal(Q̄/Q) should have trivial centre via abelian extensions, and refers to Kerckhoff's solution of the Nielsen realization problem. This page summarizes class field theory as background.

(1) Reference: Tate, 'Number theoretic background', Corvallis, Proc. Symp. Pure Math. 33, part 2 (1979), pp. 3-26, with §1 on pp. 3-9.

(2) Local class field theory for a local field K:
- Gal(K̄/K)^ab ≅ the profinite completion of K*.
- Better: W(K̄/K)^ab ≅ K*. Here the Weil group W is the subgroup of Gal(K̄/K) inducing an integral power of Frobenius on the residue field.
- The reciprocity map W(K̄/K) → K* is compatible with two maps to Z: on the Weil group side, the exponent of the geometric Frobenius on the residue field; on K*, the valuation. This is Deligne's normalization, in which a uniformizer corresponds to geometric Frobenius.
- Functoriality for a finite extension L/K: the transfer W(K̄/K)^ab → W(K̄/L)^ab corresponds to the inclusion K* ⊂ L*. The inclusion W(K̄/L) ⊂ W(K̄/K) corresponds to the norm N: L* → K*.

(3) Global class field theory: the same statements hold with K* replaced by the idele class group A*/K*. For a function field over F_q, W(K̄/K)^ab ↔ A*/K*. The 'degree' map to Z on the Weil group (action on the algebraic closure of the constant field) matches log_q of the idelic norm |·|. The number field case, with π_0 of the idele class group, follows on the next page, together with ray class groups, Chevalley's congruence-subgroup theorem for S-units, local-global compatibility, and the Shimura–Taniyama theory of complex multiplication.

Purpose: to give Grothendieck a concise toolkit for (a) the triviality of centres of open subgroups of the absolute Galois group of a number field, and (b) the arithmetic of CM, relevant to Galois actions on Teichmüller/moduli objects.
errors: No mathematical errors. The statements are standard and correctly normalized: geometric Frobenius corresponds to the valuation, transfer to inclusion, and inclusion of Weil groups to the norm. The equalities are, as usual, shorthand for the reciprocity isomorphism. For the global function field case, 'W^ab ↔ A*/K*' is an isomorphism onto A*/K* via the Weil group, which is correct.

ideas.what: Local reciprocity via the Weil group, W(K̄/K)^ab ≅ K*, compatible with Frobenius degree and valuation (geometric Frobenius normalization)
ideas.modern_name: Local class field theory / Weil group (Deligne's normalization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin, Hasse, Weil (1951); normalization as in Deligne's 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles des fonctions L' and Tate's Corvallis article

ideas.what: Functoriality of reciprocity: transfer corresponds to inclusion, restriction to a subgroup corresponds to the norm
Global function field reciprocity W(K̄/K)^ab ≅ A*/K*, with degree matching log_q of the idelic norm
ideas.modern_name: Global class field theory for function fields / Weil group
ideas.where_published: Artin–Tate, Class Field Theory; Tate Corvallis

missed.claim: Historical rather than mathematical: in 1981-82 Deligne coached Grothendieck by letter on class field theory, and on CM on the next page, as input for his anabelian/Teichmüller programme. This includes the argument, on the previous page, that open subgroups of G_Q have trivial centre. It documents the exchange behind the 'Esquisse'-era anabelian ideas. The mathematics itself is textbook.
missed.quote: Voici déjà le fascicule de résultat sur le corps de classes. Pour le corps de classe lui-même, une référence concise est le §1 de Tate
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Useful for the history of anabelian geometry: it shows which arithmetic input Grothendieck sought from Deligne. It contains no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine expository summary of local and global class field theory with Weil groups, written by Deligne for Grothendieck. It has only minor historical interest as a document of their 1981 correspondence.
transcription_corrections: Salutation: 'Cher Schurik' (Russian diminutive of Alexander), not 'Cher Schmik[?]'; the letter is from Pierre Deligne to Grothendieck.
'le fascicule de résultats sur le corps de classes'.
Reference: Proc. of Symposia in Pure Math. 33 (79), AMS (Corvallis, vol. 2), pp. 3-26.
Local diagram label: 'quelle puissance de F géométrique sur le corps résiduel', a left vertical arrow W(K̄/K) → Z, with the right arrow K* → Z labelled 'valuation'.

Second local diagram: the arrow W(K̄/L) → W(K̄/K) is an inclusion (hooked arrow), and N: L* → K*. In the first diagram the transfer W(K̄/K)^ab → W(K̄/L)^ab corresponds to the inclusion K* ⊂ L* (hooked arrow, not an integral sign).
Global label: 'effet sur la clôture alg. du corps des constantes'.
